documents.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is almost absent from the foundation-model literature. On OpenNeuro, the largest open BIDS-structured neuroimaging repository, fNIRS accounts for 1.0% of participants and 1.6% of datasets, against 28.6 times more participants for EEG. We ask why, and what a first fNIRS foundation model would require. The paper is a review and a roadmap: its contribution is an inventory, a synthesis of evidence from adjacent modalities, and a set of requirements, not new model results.We argue that the barrier is not primarily data structure. The fNIRS data standards already require sensor positions to be recorded, so the laborious step of reconstructing where each sensor sat, which dominates the equivalent EEG models, is largely unnecessary here. The barrier is corpus scale, compounded by the absence of any clinical archive comparable to the Temple University Hospital EEG corpus, and by the recency of NIRS-BIDS, published in 2025 against 2019 for EEG. Because no single fNIRS corpus is large enough, aggregation across heterogeneous montages is the most plausible route to pretraining scale, which makes montage-agnostic architecture a precondition rather than an optimization.Reviewing four EEG foundation models that solve montage heterogeneity, we find that the two available ablations of both components rank spatial aggregation above the choice of positional encoding. Several models without a unifying spatial abstraction fall to near-chance under stringent cross-montage evaluation, mainly when encoders are frozen or tested on layouts they were not trained on. In hemodynamic and multimodal work, the one foundation model borrowed from another domain gave no uplift on fNIRS, while joint pretraining with EEG did. In the one available ablation, though, that benefit tracked the mutual information between modalities and, at the larger shot counts, fell below fNIRS-only pretraining at the lowest level tested. From functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) we take a direction fNIRS has not yet followed: recent work there has moved from signal reconstruction toward latent prediction, because the signal is noisy and off-the-shelf evaluation matters. That rationale may be particularly relevant to fNIRS, where some of the systemic physiological confounds, particularly the Mayer wave, overlap the band in which the hemodynamic signal is analyzed. We chart the nine fNIRS-relevant works we located. We identify three especially consequential properties of fNIRS with no electrophysiological counterpart (source–detector geometry, chromophore choice and hemodynamic timescale) and set out eight requirements for a first fNIRS foundation model, on which work is under way in our laboratory.

Enterprises pour billions into artificial intelligence, yet half of the models never see a real user. Discover why machine learning projects stall before deployment and how product teams can bridge the gap between complex data artifacts and the actual decisions users need to drive real business value. Full article: https://davidohnstad.net/why-most-ml-models-never-reach-production/

Financial sustainability is a growing concern for Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). Many institutions face structural financial pressures due to reduced public funding, volatile enrolment, and rising costs. Although institutions collect increasing amounts of financial data, sustainability assessments often rely on backward-looking accounting ratios and provide limited insight into future patterns. Rather than proposing a new machine-learning algorithm, this study integrates and empirically evaluates established, complementary analytical techniques within one framework: financial Key Performance Indicator (KPI) engineering, a Financial Sustainability Index (FSI), machine-learning prediction, relative sustainability classification, institutional clustering, anomaly detection, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Using the public Higher Education Statistics Agency finance collection, we constructed a longitudinal dataset containing 2207 provider-year observations and examined income diversification, funding dependency, research activity, growth, and capital investment. Supervised prediction was evaluated on 1880 longitudinal records using leakage-safe expanding-window temporal validation. Across 1387 out-of-time observations, the persistence baseline achieved the strongest performance, with an R2 of 0.868, an MAE of 1.332, and an RMSE of 2.462. The Random Forest model remained strongly predictive, achieving an R2 of 0.852, an MAE of 1.587, and an RMSE of 2.612, while demonstrating stable performance across 30 random seeds. Temporal relative-sustainability classification achieved a mean accuracy of 0.842 and a macro-F1 score of 0.835. Unsupervised analysis identified three institutional profiles, while Isolation Forest flagged 111 financially atypical provider-year observations. Once current-year FSI was excluded, XAI analysis identified tuition dependency, income diversification, unrestricted reserves, and premises costs as the indicators on which predictions relied most. Because the FSI is internally constructed and the classification categories are sample-relative, the framework is presented as a proof-of-concept approach for sustainability screening and benchmarking rather than a validated predictor of financial distress.

Large language models are known to be sycophantic, over-complying with users even when doing so is unproductive. When these models act as coding agents, this can be costly: an agent that keeps editing after no edit improves the code writes churn, technical debt, and review burden into the codebase. Yet the consequences of sycophancy in software engineering remain largely understudied. To understand them, we run a controlled study of iterative refactoring, an open-ended task with no stopping criterion, where any edit an agent makes once the code is already clean reflects compliance rather than improvement. Across algorithmic (n=50) and object-oriented (n=10) suites, we repeatedly ask two widely used agents, Codex and Claude Code, to refactor further across five models. Over 3,000 turns, we define six behavioral signals of over-compliance. We hypothesized that a capable agent would stop once it recognized an optimized codebase; none did. Every model kept editing, rewriting up to 31x the original codebase before first stopping and resuming edits even after declaring the task complete. Over-compliance is a costly, multi-turn behavior that compounds with every turn, and our six signals give developers and tool builders a way to detect and curb it.

Monocular depth estimation has advanced rapidly with the development of foundation models that demonstrate strong zero-shot generalisation across diverse visual domains. However, the applicability of these models to visual perception for lower-limb prosthetics remains largely unexplored. Reliable depth perception is particularly important for prosthesis users, who often experience significant challenges when navigating stairs, uneven terrain, and other complex environments. To address this gap, we introduce the Lower-Limb Prosthesis (LP) dataset, a benchmark designed to evaluate depth perception from an emulated knee-level prosthetic viewpoint. Using this dataset, we evaluate four state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation foundation models. Our results provide the first systematic benchmark of monocular depth estimation performance from a prosthetic viewpoint, while highlighting both the challenges and the potential of deploying foundation models in prosthetic perception systems. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Ishivijay/lp_dataset.

This academic article aims to 1) synthesize concepts and theories explaining sustainable school administration in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), 2) analyze the opportunities and risks of AI in each domain of school administration, and 3) propose a model and recommendations for school administrators and policymakers. The author conducted an integrative literature review and qualitative document analysis of 44 documents, organized by Thailand's four domains of school administration (academic affairs, personnel, budget, and general administration), using sustainable leadership, sociotechnical systems theory, and TPACK as analytical lenses. The synthesis shows that AI can support personalized learning, reduce teachers' non-teaching workload, and strengthen data-informed decisions. However, school-based evidence remains limited, and AI use carries risks of privacy breaches, algorithmic bias, digital inequality, and long-term costs. The article proposes the SAISA Model (Sustainable AI-Integrated School Administration), comprising inputs, four administrative processes anchored by data governance, outputs, sustainability outcomes, and an assessment-and-learning feedback loop, with recommendations for school administrators, educational service area offices, and policymakers.

No-code development platforms integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) to provide opportunity for non-technical users, like entrepreneurs, to innovate in software development. However, they still necessitate a level of coding proficiency to use effectively. A case study of building a travel mobile app with low and high tech prompts in an LLM-based no-code development platform explores how to support non-technical users by mapping technical capabilities to product needs described in plain English. The low tech prompts yield variable results in successful feature implementation and can mimic functionality instead of using the needed technical capabilities. The findings from this evaluation inform prompting guidelines, supporting non-technical users in executing their business and product needs. Mapping user concepts to underlying technical capabilities can be used as a framework to support usability of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for programming applications.

Emerging 6G control planes would compose Large Language Model (LLM) agents that exchange interpreted conclusions, so hallucinations can propagate even over error-free transport. Recent architectures audit each message locally against the sender's observation mask, but isolated audits miss collective behavior. Modeling the agent society as a cellular sheaf, we establish three laws valid on arbitrary topologies. First, the \emph{composition law}: network-wide divergence exceeds the sum of per-agent audit scores by exactly their hidden total correlation. This blind spot masks up to 23\% of joint divergence and, because the declared signal cancels in the cognitive signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), overstates it by $1.14$\,dB purely through topology; the resulting trust inflation preserves valid consensus states but slows convergence. Second, the \emph{scaling law}: reconciliation decouples across metric counters, so the worst-connected dimension sets the pace. Consistency time grows for a society size $n$ as $Ω(n^{2/d})$ on polynomial-growth topologies of degree $d$, and paths breach a $1$\,s near-real-time budget at $n^\ast=13$ agents, whereas expanders ($Θ(1)$) and radius-3 local audits ($O(1)$, $\approx300$\,ms) stay bounded. Third, the \emph{consistency-time law}: the timing error from omitted correlations is one-sided and capped by the worst-measured link. These laws, validated on simulated topologies and deployed LLM societies, give provable worst-case latency ceilings for near-real-time operation.

The main aim of this study was to find the connection between perceived university fairness, resilience and academic engagement among university students in Karachi, Pakistan. The cross-sectional correlational design was used, 500 young adults (males = 121, female = 376, other = 3) aged 18 to 26 and above were selected from public, private and federally chartered universities through convenience sampling. The participants answered the University Fairness Questionnaire, Brief Resilience scale and Academic Engagement scale having 3 sub-scales including behavioral, cognitive and anxious engagement. The results via statistical analysis demonstrated that perceived university fairness has a significant negative correlation with behavioral engagement, and cognitive engagement, whereas it positively correlates with anxious engagement. Resilience showed positive correlation with cognitive engagement, a significant negative correlation with anxious engagement and no significant relationship with behavioral engagement. A significant negative correlation was found between perceived university fairness and resilience. The outcomes suggest that higher perceptions of university unfairness are linked to lower resilience and academic engagement, also increasing anxious engagement among higher education students. The research highlights the value of encouraging fairness, boosting resilience and improving student engagement alongside psychological well-being in university settings.

Precision livestock farming increasingly relies on intelligent monitoring systems to improve animal health, welfare, and farm productivity. However, conventional cloud-centric approaches often face challenges related to data privacy, communication overhead, network dependency, and real-time decision-making. This study proposes a Federated Learning (FL) and Edge-AI framework for distributed livestock health monitoring that integrates Smart Neck Collar sensing, edge computing, MQTT-based communication, and a hybrid Gradient Boosting–Long Short-Term Memory (GBoost-LSTM) prediction architecture. The proposed framework enables local preprocessing, model training, and inference at participating farms while supporting collaborative model learning without transferring raw livestock sensor data to a central server. A simulation-based federated evaluation was designed using livestock health data collected from 150 dairy cows across seven districts of Punjab, India. The proposed framework was compared with previously evaluated centralized machine-learning approaches to assess its predictive performance. The simulated FL-GBoost-LSTM model achieved an accuracy of 95.12%, precision of 93.48%, recall of 88.21%, and F1-score of 90.76% under the evaluation configuration described in this study. The results indicate that federated collaborative learning can provide competitive disease-prediction performance while retaining data locally at participating farms. In addition, the proposed edge-based architecture is designed to reduce dependence on continuous cloud connectivity and support localized health-status assessment. Because the present evaluation is simulation-based and does not constitute a field deployment, the reported communication, latency, privacy, and scalability benefits should be interpreted as framework-level findings rather than validated operational outcomes. Future work will focus on real-world multi-farm deployment, systematic non-IID evaluation, formal privacy-enhancement mechanisms, and comprehensive benchmarking of computational, communication, and energy requirements. Proposed a Federated Learning and Edge-AI framework for distributed livestock health monitoring across geographically separated dairy farms. Integrated Smart Neck Collar sensing, MQTT-based communication, edge computing, and hybrid GBoost-LSTM prediction within a unified architecture. Simulated collaborative model training across distributed farm-level datasets while retaining raw livestock data locally. Achieved 95.12% accuracy, 93.48% precision, 88.21% recall, and 90.76% F1-score under the reported simulation-based evaluation configuration. Compared the proposed federated framework with previously evaluated centralized livestock disease-prediction models to assess predictive performance. Identified communication efficiency, edge inference, non-IID data handling, privacy enhancement, and real-world deployment as key areas requiring further experimental validation.

PURPOSE: The use of gamification-based educational interventions in dentistry has been proposed as a novel approach to increase cognitive engagement and improve learning; however, evidence regarding the simultaneous effect of these tools on students' knowledge and attitude in the field of orthodontics is limited. This study evaluated the usability of a gamified orthodontic application and compared its knowledge and attitude outcomes with traditional reference-book study. METHODS: In an experimental study, 80 sixth-year dental students were assigned to the intervention and control groups. The intervention group used a gamified scenario-based application for 1 month. Usability was assessed with the Mobile Health App Usability Questionnaire (MAUQ). Knowledge and attitude scores were measured before and after the intervention, and data were analysed using a mixed linear model. RESULTS: The mean usability scores were assessed as satisfactory. Although both groups improved, significant time × group interactions favoured the intervention group for knowledge (p = 0.013) and attitude (p = 0.001). However, the observed effect sizes were small to moderate, suggesting a limited but potentially meaningful educational benefit. Orthodontic course grade showed a positive and significant association with both outcomes (p < 0.05), whereas gender, overall grade point average (GPA), and software usage history were not significantly associated with the outcomes (p > 0.05). CONCLUSION: Compared with traditional reference-book study, the gamified application was associated with modest improvements in knowledge and attitudes. However, the design did not allow the specific contribution of gamification to be distinguished from other digital-learning effects.

communication, and machine-learning hardware require high speed, low power consumption, and fault tolerance. This work proposes a high-speed, power-efficient, and fault-tolerant finite impulse response (FIR) filter architecture by integrating Vedic mathematics, reversible logic, and error-correction coding into an FPGA-based framework for machine-learning accelerators. A 16-tap FIR filter is implemented on a Xilinx Virtex-5 FPGA using the Urdhva-Tiryakbhayam Vedic multiplication technique with reversible Peres and controlled-NOT (CNOT) gates and a reversible look-ahead carry adder (LACA), enabling parallel computation with reduced information loss. A Hamming-code-based error correction code (ECC) module is incorporated to detect and correct single-bit soft errors without the hardware overhead associated with triple modular redundancy (TMR). Synthesis results demonstrate a propagation delay of 30.932 ns and power consumption of 2.645 mW, achieving a 5.57% latency improvement over an multiple constant multiplication (MCM)-based FIR baseline while providing single-bit fault correction. The proposed architecture demonstrates its suitability as a replacement for multiply-accumulate (MAC) units in convolutional neural network accelerators, particularly for power-constrained and fault-sensitive edge artificial intelligence applications.

Fatigue is a major safety concern in high-risk industries and can result from insufficient sleep, prolonged mental workload, and sustained physical exertion. While existing fatigue management approaches often focus on scheduling or generic interventions, they rarely provide personalized recommendations tailored to a worker’s current fatigue condition. To address this gap, a personalized fatigue mitigation recommendation system was designed to support fatigue risk management in offshore oil and gas extraction (OGE) operations. The system integrates research evidence and offshore expert consensus within a multi-criteria decision-making framework to generate individualized fatigue mitigation strategies based on workers’ fatigue profiles. The system considers four fatigue-related indicators: mental exhaustion, physical exertion, perceived sleepiness, and sleep loss. The recommendation system was applied to a real-world offshore fatigue dataset containing over 1,800 fatigue records collected from workers. Results demonstrated the feasibility of generating context-aware and personalized recommendations across a wide range of fatigue states.

Against the backdrop of digital media iteration and the expansion of China’s animation industry, aesthetic discourse surrounding female animated characters demonstrates differentiated structural features across production eras and evaluation contexts. Existing research is constrained by fragmented indicator systems, single-modality data, and a lack of standardized frameworks to support long-term cross-era quantitative comparison. To address these gaps, this study constructs a three-tier aesthetic evaluation framework consisting of Beauty of Image, Beauty of Impression, and Beauty of Idea, and proposes a dual-perspective quantitative workflow integrating large language model-based text mining, multimodal visual feature extraction, and the entropy-weighted TOPSIS method. Based on 72 representative Chinese animated works, 851,217 raw user comments, and 261 standardized character images, this study analyzes the distribution of aesthetic dimensions in both narrative-comment and pure-visual scenarios respectively, and validates the methodological reliability from three aspects: inter-annotator agreement, human–machine consistency, and test-retest stability. Quantitative results reveal that the two contexts present divergent aesthetic weight structures: identity-related dimensions exhibit the highest discriminative salience in narrative scenarios, while visual morphological attributes dominate in pure-visual settings. Across production eras, the discriminative salience of static morphological dimensions shows a steady upward trend, whereas the differentiating power of traditional cultural aesthetic dimensions declines gradually. High-frequency aesthetic vocabulary presents identity-oriented structural features in narrative contexts and form-and-style-oriented features in pure-visual scenarios respectively, with an overall evolutionary trend shifting toward visual detail orientation over time. This study empirically validates the effectiveness of the three-tier aesthetic framework and provides a standardized cross-era quantitative analytical paradigm for animation aesthetics research.

A property-based test (PBT) checks a property of a program on many generated inputs, but writing one takes a property, a generator of valid inputs, and an oracle. LLM-based PBT writers produce all three, yet they have been evaluated only on Python libraries. We study how two of them, Proptest-AI and Agentic-PBT, generalize to ten programs in five domains: deep learning libraries, databases, system software, compilers, and LLM serving engines. Most of these programs take text in their own language, such as queries, configurations, and programs. Agentic-PBT covers more branches than Proptest-AI on seven of the ten programs with Opus 5 and on all ten with GLM-5.3-Flash. Domain-specific fuzzers cover more of the compilers and of PostgreSQL and less of PyTorch than Agentic-PBT. We filed 180 bug reports, 44 of which duplicate reports that others filed after the models' knowledge cutoffs; maintainers have confirmed 65 of the others, in all five domains, and fixed 23. We draw lessons for building and evaluating such writers: low observability hurts them, and mature fuzzers paired with LLM-written properties could check that each feature behaves as documented.

We evaluated a pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) psychiatry collaborative intervention designed to streamline mental and behavioral health (MBH) patient management and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS). Using electronic health record (EHR) data from 151,014 pediatric emergency department (PED) visits at a single urban PED in South Carolina between October 1, 2017, and November 30, 2023, we evaluated an intervention implemented on April 1, 2023 in which PEM physicians performed initial evaluations and promptly consulted psychiatry post-medical stabilization. Psychiatry then managed stable MBH patients through discharge or inpatient admission. An interrupted time series analysis with an ARIMA model assessed LOS among 8,791 pediatric MBH patients. The intervention system significantly reduced LOS by 81.3 min for MBH patients in the PED ( p < .001). Future research should replicate this intervention in diverse healthcare settings to assess generalizability and further refine strategies for improving care for pediatric MBH patients.
topics: Psychiatric care and mental health services

documents.abstract: Aircraft assembly requires repeatedly performing precision tasks at various heights and non-neutral positions. Prolonged exposure to non-neutral positions is a risk factor for work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). Traditional ergonomic assessments can support quantifying these risks, but are time consuming. Wearable motion sensing from Inertial Measurement Units (IMU) could support ergonomists quantifying postural exposure across work shifts. This study evaluated alignment between Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) shoulder and torso scores from a focus group of ergonomists and an IMU-based analysis using data collected from a worker performing assembly tasks. The proof-of-concept results suggest the proposed method is promising for identifying general postural exposure trends. Differences in expert perceptions and IMU-based analysis were observed, which could arise from the video format of the observations, including the point of view of the worker or the visual context. Further investigation should consider how to present IMU-based data to support ergonomist decision-making needs.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Overhead and awkward postures in assembly can shift muscular demands and accelerate localized fatigue. While electromyography (EMG) amplitude and frequency features are commonly used to assess fatigue, these features can be difficult to interpret independently. This proof-of-concept study applied the Joint Analysis of Spectrum and Amplitude (JASA) method to characterize biceps and triceps fatigue for select assembly-relevant tasks at three different heights using data from one experienced worker. For each task, slopes of root mean square (RMS) and median frequency were computed and mapped to JASA categories. Initial findings indicate fatigue patterns consistent with expectations associated with the task, height, and arm usage. Elevated height was more frequently associated with dominant triceps fatigue, with nominal and lowered heights more often associated with dominant biceps fatigue. The JASA method provides insight into disambiguating force increase/decrease from fatigue behavior and should be further evaluated to support ergonomic interventions in assembly work.

Automotive human factors knowledge is essential for early design decisions, yet relevant evidence is often dispersed across standards, design guidelines, regulatory resources, and research-based evidence. Designers must interpret these materials and translate them into actionable recommendations, which can limit timely use during conceptual design. This paper proposes a RAG–LLM-based method for automotive human factors design guidance. The method builds a task-oriented knowledge base from curated human factors materials, parses natural-language design inputs into structured intents, retrieves relevant evidence through semantic and terminology-based matching, and generates structured recommendations with source attribution. A prototype system demonstrated the workflow through a representative automotive HMI case, transforming an open-ended route-entry design task into evidence-grounded recommendations with inspectable sources. Preliminary user-oriented evaluation suggested usefulness for knowledge access, recommendation interpretation, and evidence review, indicating potential to support early-stage design reasoning.

Artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved from a specialist computing capability into a general-purpose technology used in customer service, marketing, finance, operations, information management, software development, and decision support. For small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies, these tools can create meaningful opportunities to improve productivity and service delivery. However, the conditions under which SMEs adopt AI are often very different from those of large firms and highly digitized economies. This paper develops a responsible AI adoption framework for SMEs in developing economies, with particular attention to Uganda, and grounds it in secondary data drawn from international and national reports and statistics. Global evidence shows that AI adoption has accelerated sharply, with 72% of surveyed organizations reporting AI use and 65% regularly using generative AI in at least one business function in 2024 (McKinsey & Company, 2024). In Uganda, however, internet penetration stood at 28.0% of the population and access to electricity at roughly 30% in recent measurements (DataReportal, 2025; International Energy Agency [IEA], 2023), while micro, small, and medium enterprises make up about 90% of private-sector production yet report only 35% technology adoption, with 53.4% of owners possessing neither a smartphone nor a computer (Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives [MTIC], 2024). This contrast is the empirical core of the paper: access alone does not explain or guarantee responsible AI adoption. The framework brings together the Technology-Organization- Environment (TOE) perspective, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), responsible AI governance principles, cybersecurity requirements, and the development context reflected in recent Ugandan policy materials. Six dimensions are proposed: technological readiness, organizational readiness, human capability, data readiness, environmental conditions, and responsible AI governance.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: The rapid growth of internet of things (IoT) applications has generated an urgent demand for efficient task scheduling mechanisms that feature low latency, scalability, and resource awareness. While fog computing can meet this demand by extending computing and storage resources to the vicinity of data sources, it still confronts four core challenges: resource heterogeneity, dynamic workloads, mobility, and security constraints. To address these issues, this study conducts a systematic review of intelligent task scheduling for fog-enabled IoT systems. It classifies the included eligible studies into five scheduling paradigms, and innovatively proposes a cross-domain framework that integrates three types of awareness, including priority awareness. The subsequent work of this study will sort out the core strengths and limitations of existing relevant methods. Finally, open challenges and emerging research directions, including edge artificial intelligence (AI), federated learning, blockchain-assisted scheduling, and hardware-accelerated implementations are discussed. The findings provide useful guidance for developing scalable, secure, and adaptive scheduling frameworks for next-generation fog-enabled IoT systems.

Large Language Models(LLMs) have shown strong performance on tasks with verifiable answers, but many real-world queries involve subjectivity, disagreement, and conflicting evidence. Most existing benchmarks for such queries remain English-centric, overlooking the vast diversity of perspectives held by users worldwide. To systematically study how LLM perspectives vary across languages, we curate PerspectivesQA, a manually verified multilingual dataset of globally contested topics covering 18 languages, and propose ROOTS, a framework that profiles linguistic, perspective, and framing diversity. We evaluate a diverse set of eight models covering both open-source and proprietary families at varying scales, establishing that LLMs hedge their answers in English but commit to positions in lower-resource languages. Larger models maintain a more consistent cross-lingual worldview, while smaller models are more easily swayed. All models also exhibit high sensitivity to minor surface-level input variations, producing notable stance even in larger models.

Independent mobility is essential to the daily lives of the growing population of people who are blind or visually impaired (PBVI). Although research on assistive mobility has expanded rapidly, limitations and challenges identified through empirical evaluations remain insufficiently synthesized. This scoping review examines 50 studies to investigate how PBVI wayfinding and navigation approaches have been empirically evaluated and to synthesize their reported shortcomings. In this review, wayfinding refers to route planning and environmental understanding, whereas navigation refers to real-time movement during travel. Four recurring themes emerged: device appearance, hardware and software performance, user interaction, and integration into daily life. We further identify critical questions that highlight gaps between existing approaches and user expectations. Based on these themes and cross-study implications, we develop a practical checklist that translates concerns from prior evaluations into actionable considerations for the future design and evaluation of assistive mobility technologies for PBVI.
topics: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

documents.abstract: Physical rehabilitation helps patients recover from injury and regain functional independence, but social and structural determinants of health, including living conditions, income, and transportation, can limit access to in-person care. Telerehabilitation addresses many of these barriers by enabling patients to complete therapy at home while supporting remote monitoring. However, the lack of direct supervision may reduce patient engagement, motivation, and adherence to prescribed exercises. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) offer opportunities to develop adaptive, personalized rehabilitation systems that enhance the effectiveness of self-directed therapy. This scoping review examines current developments in AI-driven rehabilitation, focusing on the techniques used, evaluation methods employed, and user experiences reported across studies. By synthesizing recent research, the review identifies emerging trends, common challenges, and opportunities for future AI-enabled telerehabilitation systems that improve patient engagement and support long-term rehabilitation outcomes.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This study examined whether tactile detection reduces dual-task costs compared to visual detection when paired with a visual tracking task, and whether this advantage persists as temporal task load increases. Thirty-eight participants completed a visual tracking task and a detection task concurrently. The detection task was presented either visually or tactually, and temporal task load was manipulated by varying the stimulus presentation rate. Performance was analyzed using signal detection theory measures to determine whether differences between visual and tactile detection reflected changes in perceptual sensitivity, response bias, or both. Tactile detection produced smaller dual-task costs than visual detection across hit rate, false alarm rate, sensitivity, and response bias. Critically, tactile detection better preserved sensitivity under dual-task conditions, suggesting reduced perceptual competition with the visual tracking task. However, higher temporal load still degraded performance in the tactile condition. These findings support multimodal interface design while highlighting limits of modality diversification.

Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.
topics: Thermodynamic and Structural Properties of Metals and Alloys

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) image-to-video systems have lowered the technical threshold for presenting traditional cultural content in motion, while generated motion may alter characters, props, narrative relationships, craft features, composition, and symbols. This study implements a trustworthiness assessment workflow for traditional narrative images in architectural decoration, linking cultural evidence dossiers, sample-adapted prompts, computer-vision measurements, and blinded human coding. Eight source images were used to generate 120 videos under three prompt conditions, with five outputs per image–condition cell. Four coders assessed the videos, five experts reviewed the coding instrument, and two new coders independently assessed 48 videos. Primary deviation rates were 7.12%, 7.37%, and 9.07% for conditions A, B, and C, respectively, with no significant blocked difference after correction (Friedman χ2(2) = 1.400; Holm-adjusted p = 1.000). Mean item-level Krippendorff’s alpha was 0.250 across 14 estimable items; the independent-review composite ICC (A,1) was 0.402. Additional analyses examined coder sensitivity and the grouped generation structure. The original association involving inter-frame stability SSIM was not supported in within-image–condition comparisons (ρ = −0.052; permutation p = 0.610). An exploratory association was observed between source-image SSIM and human-coded deviations within these cells (ρ = −0.366; Holm-adjusted permutation p = 0.021). The study provides a documented procedure for comparing generated outputs and identifies limits in prompt effectiveness and the reproducibility of human judgments.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: Generative AI interfaces can insert sponsored content at multiple points in an answer, where click-through rates (CTRs) depend on the advertiser-position pair. Under the cascade model, users read ads sequentially and stop after their first click, so both ad assignment and display order affect welfare. For arbitrary pair-specific CTRs, Balseiro et al. (WWW 2026) gave a $4/(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation whose monotonicity has not been established, and a monotone $O(\log m)$-approximation for $m$ candidate positions. Earlier truthful constant-factor mechanisms require factorized CTR models and do not apply. Whether monotonicity is compatible with a constant-factor approximation in this general setting was left open by that work. We give a polynomial-time mechanism for arbitrary pair-specific CTRs and any limit on displayed ads that is truthful and individually rational in expectation and achieves a 2-approximation to optimal cascade welfare. Our mechanism selects an advertiser-position matching and a designated last ad, then randomly thins earlier ads so that each selected ad's expected cascade CTR is the same fraction of its standalone CTR. This yields an exact closed-form expression for expected welfare, which we maximize over a bid-independent lottery range using linear programming. Exact optimization ensures monotonicity, while a random-prefix decomposition proves the factor-two guarantee, which is tight for this range. We also show that exactly optimizing the previous welfare surrogate can violate monotonicity, and evaluate welfare and running time on synthetic instances.

As Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research continues to expand rapidly, synthesizing evidence on AD determinants across large scientific databases has become increasingly difficult at scale. This verification study compares human manual extraction with a Large Language Model (LLM) approach for identifying AD determinants from 10 systematic reviews retrieved from the Web of Science database. Two parallel extraction workflows were applied to the same source material. The human researcher identified 81 distinct determinants, whereas the LLM identified 74, with 44 human determinants and 41 LLM determinants overlapping across both approaches. While both methods showed strong alignment on well-established behavioral and lifestyle risk factors, the LLM frequently consolidated clinically distinct variables into broader umbrella categories, a pattern termed lossy consolidation. Although the LLM demonstrated major advantages in efficiency and quantitative evidence retrieval, the findings support hybrid evidence-synthesis workflows in which LLM extraction is combined with targeted human validation to preserve determinant-level clinical specificity.

Achieving Super Artificial Intelligence by 2028 A Three-Model Collaborative Architecture Based on a Memory System, Swarm Intelligence, and Real-Time Learning Author: William (Superintelligence Researcher and Architect) Abstract This paper proposes a system architecture for Super Artificial General Intelligence (SAGI) aimed at practical deployment by 2028. Driven by three core engines—the Physical Space Model (PSM), the Causal Reasoning Model (CRM), and the Decision & Verification Model (DVM)—and supported by three foundational infrastructure layers: the Memory System, Swarm Intelligence, and Real-Time Learning Intelligence, this architecture constructs a general-purpose intelligent agent capable of generating outputs with a near-100% probability of correctness. This paper details the design principles, collaborative mechanisms, and engineering implementation pathways for each module, providing a comprehensive technical blueprint for transitioning Super Artificial General Intelligence from theoretical concepts to real-world engineering deployment.

Epileptic seizures affect approximately 1% of the global population, causing significant physical, cognitive, and psychological harm. Existing detection methods identify seizures only after onset, offering limited time for clinical intervention. Furthermore, most models rely on publicly available datasets and operate on resource-heavy architectures that cannot be deployed on wearable devices. This research proposes a novel Adaptive Pre-Ictal SLT-SNN framework that predicts epileptic seizures before onset, adapts to individual patient patterns, operates efficiently on low-power devices, and is validated on locally collected clinical EEG data from Pakistan. The proposed model integrates Slantlet Transform (SLT) for enhanced feature extraction with Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) for biologically inspired, energy-efficient classification. A novel adaptive learning mechanism enables the model to personalize predictions without full retraining. Validated on both standard benchmarks (CHB-MIT, UCI-ESR) and local de-identified clinical data, the framework achieves 97.2% pre-ictal prediction accuracy and maintains 94.8% accuracy on unseen patients, while reducing computational complexity by 62% compared to baseline models.
